newsitem.title: UK: Brent CFDs bounce in flat North Sea crude market.
newsitem.headline: Brent CFDs bounce in flat North Sea crude market.

text.p: Buoyant Brent Contracts for Difference (CFDs) created the only ripples in a mostly becalmed North Sea crude market on Thursday, traders said.
Prompt CFDs (May 27-30) gained three cents to trade at July Brent -7 cents and were bid even firmer at -3 cents by midday. Later weeks followed suit, June 2-6 at July Brent -10/-5 cents.
CFDs continued to benefit from tight supply of Brent, Forties and other North Sea grades in the first half of next month, traders said.
Talk that U.S. refiner Koch was looking to buy another Dated cargo loading in the first decade of June also lifted sentiment.
IPE July Brent gained six cents to $20.19 a barrel but intermonth paper spreads were little changed, June/July fetching +7 cents in line with late U.S. trade on Wednesday.
Shipping brokers said Koch fixed the Hellespont Paramount to load 365,000 tonnes of Brent at Sullom Voe around June 6.
Traders said Koch needed to buy another cargo to fill the vessel, from which three had already been sold into the U.S. Gulf and a further two were destined for its own system.
With only one June 6-8 Brent turning wet on Thursday and most other cargoes with suitable dates committed to a European major's system, Dated Brent was expected to remain firm.
North Sea sentiment also drew support from thin supply of other grades, notably Forties and Oseberg which had their loading programmes for early June decimated by scheduled maintenance work.
Poor refining margins kept some buyers at bay but a slight pick-up in returns this week appeared to prompt most refiners to delay decisions on trimming crude throughput.
"Margins are absolutely dire at the moment but we haven't done anything about reducing runs yet, we're still monitoring the situation," said a trader for a leading European refiner.
